name: Jeshohaiah
overview: Jeshohaiah is a male figure identified as a member of the tribe of Simeon in Scripture. His unique attribute is noted with uncertainty in 1 Chronicles 4:36, where he is listed among Simeonites. There are no additional notes or detailed descriptions about his life or role.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeshohaiah appears once in Scripture and is understood to possibly mean 'Yahweh humbles.' This reflects a theocentric meaning common in Hebrew names, though the exact significance is not expanded upon in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Jeshohaiah is explicitly recorded as a descendant of Simeon, linking him to one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Beyond this tribal affiliation, Scripture does not provide further family relationships or lineage details for him.
scriptureSignificance: Jeshohaiah's mention in 1 Chronicles situates him within the genealogical records that affirm the continuity of God's covenant people through the tribe of Simeon. Though not highlighted for specific deeds, his presence in the biblical genealogies underscores the faithfulness of God in preserving the tribes of Israel. His listing contributes to the broader biblical narrative that culminates in the coming of Christ through Israel.
